system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering Apple (AAPL) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: Sector Update: Tech Stocks Mixed Friday Afternoon

BODY:
01:57 PM EST, 01/02/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Tech stocks were mixed Friday afternoon, with the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) easing 0.3% and the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) gaining 3.2%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index jumped 3.5%.

In corporate news, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) shares rose 5.1% after Reuters reported Wednesday the company received an annual license from the US government to move chip manufacturing equipment to its sites in Nanjing, China.

Apple (AAPL) scaled back production and marketing initiatives around its Vision Pro headset amid a failure to attract customers, the Financial Times reported Thursday. Apple shares fell 0.9%.

Baidu (BIDU) shares surged 14%. The company plans to spin off its Kunlunxin chip division and list the unit's shares on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
</article>

<summary>
Tech stocks were mixed Friday, with the broader sector index (XLK) slipping 0.3% while semiconductors outperformed—XSD jumped 3.2% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor index rose 3.5%, partly boosted by TSMC's 5.1% gain after securing a US license for China chip equipment transfers. Apple shares fell 0.9% following a Financial Times report that the company is scaling back production and marketing of its Vision Pro headset due to weak customer demand, signaling continued softness in Apple's mixed-reality ambitions. Meanwhile, Baidu surged 14% on plans to spin off its Kunlunxin chip unit for a Hong Kong listing. Apple also announced a new $5 billion share buyback program.
</summary>

or speculative links to AAPL that the article does not make.
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about AAPL in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported
ticker_focus  (does it tell a AAPL analyst what matters, and represent how central AAPL really is?)

  3 a generic article summary; the AAPL angle is implicit or buried
  1 ignores AAPL, or implies the article is about / important for AAPL when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse

  "overstates_ticker_link": true | false,
  "faithfulness": 1-5,
  "ticker_focus": 1-5,
  "coverage": 1-5,
  "conciseness": 1-5
}
